calculation_summary: STAGE 1 - FULL-CONTACT BASELINE. Anchoring to the closest matching retrieved baselines (orange: mass 154.17 g, roughness 1068.18, force 0.38 N; leather sunglasses case: mass 179.9 g, roughness 2014.79, force 1.906 N). Interpolating between these baselines for query mass 157.55 g and higher roughness 2415.65 yields a full-contact baseline estimate of approximately 0.65 N. STAGE 2 - WITHIN-SURFACE CONTACT ADJUSTMENT. The query projected contact fraction is 0.1 (significantly reduced from 1.0). Applying a monotonic non-decreasing contact adjustment multiplier for low contact fraction scales the baseline up to account for sparse contact area, resulting in 1.25 N.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: Assumption that the dry pebbled rind behaves similarly in friction and adhesion trends to leather and organic citrus peel baselines.
Uncertainty in precise scaling of contact fraction since no direct within-surface variant delta was supplied for this exact query object.
High roughness index (2415.65) degrades gecko dry adhesion performance, increasing reliance on normal force.
reasoning_trace: In Stage 1, the query object's mass (157.55 g) and roughness index (2415.65) are compared against retrieved baselines. The orange provides a clean organic baseline, while the leather sunglasses case provides a textured pebbled baseline with higher roughness. Interpolating between these neighbors yields a baseline full-contact normal force estimate of about 0.65 N. In Stage 2, the projected contact fraction is extremely low at 0.1, indicating that only a small portion of the pad makes contact due to local curvature of the pebbled organic rind and rigid pads. Following the rule that contact reduction increases required normal force monotonically, the baseline force is adjusted upward to 1.25 N. The grip remains feasible via frictional support and limited adhesion on the textured rind.
